result.title: Structure-Aware Message Passing on Petri Nets through Directed Walks and Incidence Diffusion
result.summary: A common application of the process mining discipline is to connect observed event data with Petri nets, which are bipartite, directed graphical process models with rich formal underpinnings. Recent work learns vector representations of Petri nets to retrieve process models and relate them to event logs, but leaves implicit two key aspects hidden within the net's structure: directed cycles (process loops) and invariants recorded by the net's incidence matrix. We expose both of these to message-passing graph neural networks, through a positional encoding built from return probabilities of directed place-transition walks (PNRWPE), and through same-type messages gated by diffusion kernels of the incidence matrix (DA-PNGNN). Our constructions raise macro balanced accuracy in predicting the generation factors of the 96 Process Discovery Contest 2023 models from 0.751 to 0.796 with PNRWPE, which nearly doubles accuracy on process loops, and to 0.830 with DA-PNGNN, which, without retuning, also improves net-to-tree retrieval top-1 accuracy on the self-supervised ProcRosetta benchmark by 4.1 to 5.9 points.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为 Petri 网学习向量表示，提出基于有向 place-transition 游走返回概率的位置编码 PNRWPE，以及用关联矩阵扩散核门控同类消息的 DA-PNGNN，提升生成因子预测与网到树检索效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 有向环返回概率编码与关联矩阵扩散门控，可能为 latent 循环计算中的状态重访识别、停止判断和结构化消息传递提供可核查线索，但领域与视觉推理相距较远。
